investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T09:40–09:47Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach any ready VM to satisfy the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none match the pod's node affinity or selector rules, so preemption is also impossible. Because no pod can be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returns a running VM, and the eval runner produces an empty evidence object, violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in check-expectations.json line 256. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed on 2026-07-09 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the production cluster's 6 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (only 2 nodes carry this resource, both exhausted) and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any runtime evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported it as exhausted ("Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. Preemption was also unavailable on both node sets. This is a cluster-level infrastructure constraint, not an application code defect. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with type "remote" (line 1918), which triggers remote VM provisioning; that provisioning depends on kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity being available. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created and no runtime evidence was produced, causing the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be entirely unmet.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the kata peer-pods nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new remote agent pod.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, and those 2 are already at capacity, making the cluster effectively full for this workload class.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval runs: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion would produce exactly this failure pattern across all three sibling checks.

Lower confidence — node affinity configuration drift: a change to the pod's node selector or affinity rules (not evidenced in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges) could have narrowed the eligible node set, but no such change is present in the supplied evidence.
